copy.headline: German court jails two men arrested in Aarhus over Iran plot against Jewish leaders

extended.text: Hamburg's highest court on Thursday convicted two men arrested in Denmark of preparing antisemitic attacks in Germany on behalf of Iran. Ali Hassan Sarwari, 54, a Danish citizen of Afghan background, got eight and a half years in prison; Tawab Mohsini, 43, an Afghan citizen, got four and a half.

The court found the two had watched Josef Schuster, head of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, and Volker Beck, chairman of the German-Israeli Society. They were convicted of spying for Iran, attempted complicity in murder and aggravated arson. The sentences match the prosecution's demand.
According to Der Spiegel, a German news magazine, Sarwari had also prepared an arson attack on a kosher grocery in Berlin.
Sarwari was arrested in Aarhus in June 2025 on a German warrant.
'The trial has strikingly shown how Iran exports its terror to Germany,' Beck told Bild. He wants Iran's ambassador expelled at once.

copy.headline: Supreme Court rules AI images of child abuse are punishable as real ones

standard.text: AI-generated images of child sexual abuse are as illegal and punishable as real ones, the Supreme Court ruled on Thursday. It upheld a prison term of one year and six months, none of it suspended, for a 31-year-old man from Randers, a town in Jutland, who admitted making 36,209 images with artificial intelligence and spreading them online.
His lawyer had argued that the criminal code's ban on 'depictions or the like of persons under 18' does not cover AI images of people who appear to be children.
It is the first such case to reach the Supreme Court. Red Barnet, a children's rights organisation, welcomed the ruling.

short.text: AI-generated images of child sexual abuse are as punishable as real ones, the Supreme Court ruled on Thursday. It upheld a prison term of one year and six months for a man from Randers, a town in Jutland, who made 36,209 such images.

copy.headline_short: AI abuse images punished as real
copy.deck: A man who admitted making 36,209 such images must serve one year and six months in prison.

copy.headline: EU's president will redraft the budget after leaders split over its size

standard.text: António Costa, president of the European Council, concluded at Thursday's summit in Brussels that he must present a new draft of the EU budget. Ireland, which holds the EU presidency, presented its proposal less than a week earlier, on Saturday. An EU diplomat expects the new draft within weeks.

Six countries, Denmark among them, want the Irish plan cut sharply and more spent on defence and competitiveness. Seventeen mainly southern and eastern members want a large budget that protects farm and regional aid. The Finance Ministry estimates the plan would raise Denmark's contribution by 12.7 billion kroner a year. Several EU diplomats say a deal can still be reached before Christmas.

short.text: António Costa, president of the European Council, will present a new EU budget draft after Thursday's summit showed deep division. Denmark is among six countries that want the Irish proposal cut; the Finance Ministry estimates it would raise Denmark's contribution by 12.7 billion kroner a year.

copy.deck: Denmark is among six countries that want the Irish proposal cut; it would add 12.7 billion kroner a year to Denmark's bill.

copy.headline: Nordea shares fall more than 7 per cent after the bank pauses its buyback

standard.text: Shares in Nordea, the Nordic region's largest bank, were down 7.3 per cent at 12:50 on Thursday, the worst in C25, Denmark's leading share index, after the bank paused a share buyback that investors had expected. Third-quarter profit fell to 1,181 million euros; that and revenue of 2,968 million euros were roughly what analysts had forecast.
Nordea is waiting for the European Central Bank to settle how it should measure its risks, an answer not expected until 2027. Børsen says the buyback would have been worth about 500 million euros.
Berlingske puts the cost to shareholders at 28.2 billion kroner. Other banks' shares also fell, but by less.

short.text: Shares in Nordea, the Nordic region's largest bank, were down 7.3 per cent at 12:50 on Thursday after it paused an expected share buyback. It is waiting for the European Central Bank to settle how it should measure its risks, an answer not expected until 2027.

copy.deck: Quarterly results were roughly as forecast; the bank is waiting for the European Central Bank to settle how it measures risk, which is not expected until 2027.

copy.headline: Sweden's parliament votes down Magdalena Andersson as prime minister

standard.text: The Riksdag, Sweden's parliament, rejected Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrats' leader, as prime minister on Thursday; every party but hers voted no. It was the first such vote since the election on 13 September, which gave the red-green parties a narrow majority. Up to four votes may be held before a fresh election.

Andersson called the result 'entirely expected' and said it would take 'a number of' votes. Vänsterpartiet, a left-wing party, will back only a government it sits in; the Centre Party will not work with one that includes Vänsterpartiet.
The speaker, Andreas Norlén, will now consult party leaders and has hinted that Ulf Kristersson, the sitting prime minister, may be next to try.

short.text: The Riksdag, Sweden's parliament, rejected Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrats' leader, as prime minister on Thursday; every party but hers voted no. The speaker, Andreas Norlén, has hinted that Ulf Kristersson, the sitting prime minister, may be next to try.

copy.headline: Ukraine resumes strikes on Russia's oil refineries, defying Trump

standard.text: Ukraine will resume attacks on Russia's oil refineries, Volodymyr Zelensky, its president, told the Financial Times: 'The restriction is lifted. Now it is over.' On Thursday a Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, said Pavel Malkov, the region's governor.

Donald Trump said on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy sites. Zelensky says he learned of it from the media and paused strikes for three days while Russia kept bombing Ukrainian energy plants. He says the US threatened to cut off intelligence if Ukraine did not stop.

short.text: Ukraine will resume attacks on Russia's oil refineries, Volodymyr Zelensky, its president, said, days after Donald Trump declared an energy ceasefire. On Thursday a Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, the region's governor said.

copy.deck: A Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region on Thursday, days after Donald Trump declared an energy ceasefire.
